subject: Chemistry
title: The Halifax Explosion of 1917
description: A short lesson to help you apply The Halifax Explosion of 1917.

hook.text: In 1917, a ship carrying 2,925 tons of explosives collided with another vessel in Halifax harbor—then detonated.

buildup.text: The SS Mont-Blanc was loaded with TNT, picric acid, and benzol fuel. A collision started a fire on deck.

discovery.text: The blast flattened 1,600 buildings, killed 2,000 people, and injured 9,000—the largest man-made explosion before Hiroshima.

twist.text: The blast created a tsunami that surged 18 meters above the harbor. Some survivors were then hit by a blizzard the next day.

climax.text: Halifax still sends Boston a Christmas tree each year—thanking the city for rushing emergency aid in 1917.

punchline.text: A harbor collision plus volatile cargo. The largest blast before the atomic age.

quiz.question: What made the Halifax explosion so devastating?
options: A ship carrying tons of TNT, picric acid, and fuel caught fire and detonated
A munitions factory on shore was hit by an earthquake
A submarine torpedo struck an ammunition warehouse

details.summary: In 1917 a collision in Halifax Harbor caused the French cargo ship Mont-Blanc, laden with wartime explosives including TNT and picric acid, to detonate. The explosion killed nearly 2,000 people, destroyed entire neighborhoods, and was the largest human-made explosion before nuclear weapons.
details.whyItMatters: The Halifax explosion shaped disaster preparedness, harbor safety regulations, and blast physics research. It remained the benchmark for explosive force until the atomic age.
takeaways: The Mont-Blanc carried 2,900 tons of wartime explosives
The blast destroyed a square mile of Halifax and generated a tsunami
It was the largest human-made explosion until the nuclear era

faq.question: How powerful was the Halifax explosion compared to modern bombs?
faq.answer: The Halifax explosion released energy equivalent to roughly 2.9 kilotons of TNT. For comparison, the Hiroshima atomic bomb was about 15 kilotons. Halifax was the most powerful human-made explosion for nearly three decades until nuclear weapons were tested in 1945.

faq.question: What caused the Mont-Blanc to catch fire before the explosion?
faq.answer: A collision with the Norwegian ship Imo ruptured the Mont-Blanc's hull, spilling benzol fuel that ignited. The crew, knowing the explosive cargo, abandoned ship rather than fight the fire. The burning ship drifted to shore and detonated about twenty minutes after the collision.
